stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Christopher Columbus's letter to Luis de Santangel, written in 1493 after his first voyage. Columbus wrote that the islands he found were fertile and well watered, with great rivers and trees, and that the people were gentle, timid, and well built. He wrote that the people had no weapons of iron and gave freely what they had, and that he believed gold could be found in great quantity. He told the Spanish monarchs that he had taken possession of the lands in their name.

parts.prompt: Identify one claim Columbus makes about the peoples he met.
Explain one purpose of Columbus's letter.
Explain one way Columbus's account shaped later European action in the Americas.

instruction: Answer each part in your own words from the stimulus only. Do not open the question file.
